courses.title: Anti-Money Laundering & KYC
courses.description: Anti-Money Laundering & KYC — mandatory training for Risk & Compliance.

lessons.title: What money laundering is
lessons.description:
Money laundering disguises the criminal origin of funds so they appear legitimate.

**The three stages**
- **Placement** — criminal cash enters the financial system, often in small deposits.
- **Layering** — funds move through many transactions to hide their trail.
- **Integration** — "clean" money re-enters the economy as apparently lawful wealth.

Banks are a natural target at every stage, which is why every employee has a role in prevention.

lessons.title: Red flags at the counter
lessons.description:
Be alert to activity that does not fit what you know about the customer:

- Cash deposits just under reporting thresholds (**structuring**).
- Reluctance to provide identification or source of funds.
- Rapid movement of funds in and out with no clear purpose.
- Third parties depositing into an account they do not own.
- Transactions inconsistent with the customer's stated occupation.

**Never tip off** a customer that you are suspicious — escalate quietly.

lessons.title: Knowledge check: AML basics
lessons.description: Check your understanding before moving on.

questions.prompt: Which stage moves money through many transactions to hide its origin?
Several cash deposits just below the reporting threshold suggest:
questions.explanation: Splitting deposits to avoid reporting is structuring.

questions.prompt: If you suspect a customer, you should:
questions.explanation: Tipping off is prohibited; report internally.

lessons.title: Customer due diligence
lessons.description:
KYC means knowing who your customer really is and what activity to expect.

**Standard due diligence**
- Verify identity with valid, current documents.
- Confirm address and occupation.
- Understand the purpose of the account.

**Enhanced due diligence** applies to higher-risk customers, such as politically exposed persons (PEPs), and requires senior approval and source-of-wealth checks.

lessons.title: Reporting suspicious activity
lessons.description:
When something does not add up:

1. Record what you observed, factually.
2. Submit an internal suspicious activity report to the compliance team.
3. Continue to serve the customer normally.

Compliance decides whether to file with the financial intelligence unit. Reporting in good faith protects you.

courses.title: Cybersecurity Awareness (All Staff)
courses.description: Cybersecurity Awareness (All Staff) — mandatory training for IT & Security.

lessons.title: Phishing and social engineering
lessons.description:
Most attacks start with a person, not a machine.

**Spot a phishing message**
- Urgency: "your account will be closed today".
- Mismatched sender addresses or links.
- Requests for passwords, codes or payments.

Hover over links before clicking. When in doubt, contact the sender through a channel you already trust.

lessons.title: Passwords and multi-factor authentication
lessons.description:
- Use long, unique passphrases — never reuse a work password elsewhere.
- Keep MFA on for every system that offers it.
- Never share one-time codes. The bank will never ask for them.

lessons.title: Knowledge check: cyber awareness
lessons.description: Check your understanding before moving on.

lessons.title: Clean desk and device security
lessons.description: Lock your screen whenever you step away. Keep customer documents out of sight, use approved storage only, and report lost devices immediately — fast reporting lets IT wipe them.

lessons.title: Reporting an incident
lessons.description: Clicked a suspicious link? Report it at once to the security desk. Early reports stop attacks spreading; nobody is penalised for honest mistakes reported quickly.

lessons.description: Check your understanding before moving on.

courses.title: Customer Data Privacy & Protection
courses.description: Customer Data Privacy & Protection — mandatory training for Risk & Compliance.

lessons.title: What counts as personal data
lessons.description:
Personal data is anything that identifies a person: names, ID numbers, account details, phone numbers, photos and transaction history.

Collect only what you need, use it only for the purpose it was collected for, and keep it no longer than required.

lessons.title: Handling requests and breaches
lessons.description:
- Verify identity before discussing any account.
- Share data only with authorised people, through approved channels.
- A misdirected email or lost file is a **data breach** — report it to the privacy officer the same day.

lessons.title: Knowledge check: data privacy
lessons.description: Check your understanding before moving on.

courses.title: Fraud Detection for Frontline Staff
courses.description: Fraud Detection for Frontline Staff — mandatory training for Retail Banking.

lessons.title: Common fraud schemes
lessons.description:
- **Identity fraud**: forged or borrowed documents to open accounts.
- **Account takeover**: criminals posing as the customer to change contact details.
- **Cheque and card fraud**: altered cheques, skimmed cards.
- **Authorised push-payment scams**: customers tricked into sending money themselves.

lessons.title: Protecting vulnerable customers
lessons.description: Watch for customers who seem pressured, are accompanied by someone answering for them, or want to move large sums urgently. Slow the transaction down, ask open questions, and involve a supervisor.

lessons.description: Check your understanding before moving on.

courses.title: Customer Service Excellence
courses.description: Customer Service Excellence — mandatory training for Retail Banking.

lessons.title: Listening first
lessons.description: Great service starts with understanding the need. Let the customer finish, repeat back what you heard, and agree the next step before acting.

lessons.title: Handling complaints
lessons.description:
1. Acknowledge the problem and apologise for the experience.
2. Take ownership — do not pass the customer around.
3. Explain what will happen and by when.
4. Follow up and record the complaint so it can be fixed for everyone.

courses.title: People Leadership for Managers
courses.description: People Leadership for Managers — mandatory training for HR & Learning.

lessons.title: Setting clear expectations
lessons.description: People perform best when they know what good looks like. Agree goals, explain why they matter, and check in regularly rather than only at review time.

lessons.title: Coaching and feedback
lessons.description: Give feedback soon and specifically: describe the situation, the behaviour you saw, and its impact. Ask how they see it and agree one improvement together.

lessons.title: Keeping your team compliant
lessons.description: As a manager you are accountable for your team's mandatory training. Use the manager portal to see who is overdue, send reminders, and assign what their job role requires.
